root_cause: The global keydown listener in Pikaday intercepts ArrowLeft (and other arrow keys) even when focus is in a text input that is not the calendar's field, preventing caret movement and causing the space to be appended at the end instead of inserted between characters.
repair_strategy: Add an early exit in _onKeyChange when the event target is an input, textarea, select, or contenteditable element, but only if the target is not the calendar's associated field (opts.field). This allows browser-default handling of arrow keys for other text fields while preserving calendar navigation when focus is on the field or within the picker.
expected_accessibility_effect: Arrow keys will now move the caret in text fields (like #notes) when the calendar is open, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard and 2.4.3 Focus Order, while arrow keys on the delivery date field still adjust the date as expected.
functional_risks: If the calendar's field is a contenteditable element, arrow keys would still adjust the date (may be desired).
Custom widgets that rely on arrow key handling inside inputs would need to stop propagation or implement their own handling.
verification_requirements: Pressing ArrowLeft in the #notes input while the calendar is open moves the caret left one character.
Pressing ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowDown in the #notes input still moves the caret as expected.
When focus is on the #delivery-date input, ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down still change the selected date.
When focus is on a calendar button (e.g., a day button), ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down still change the selected date.
Enter and Escape keys still close the picker when focus is on the associated field.
Typing text in the #notes input works correctly and updates the form data as intended.
